= JavaScript grammar patch provenance

Upstream: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-javascript v0.25.0,
commit `44c892e0be055ac465d5eeddae6d3e194424e7de`.
The upstream MIT licence, Rust bindings, scanner and queries are preserved.

One grammar correction: admit the existing reserved keyword terminals as
identifier aliases inside `_jsx_identifier`. JSX names do not carry
JavaScript's reserved-word exclusion. This admits SVG's `in`, keyword-named
attributes and namespaces without relaxing keywords in JavaScript statements
or attribute-value expressions. The current grammar, including modern
`using` declarations, remains in use; there is no grammar downgrade or TSX
fallback and no source rewriting.

Generated with the official tree-sitter CLI 0.27.0, native QuickJS runtime,
ABI 15: `tree-sitter generate --js-runtime native --abi 15`.
The official Linux x64 generator archive's verified SHA-256 is
`20a1f39ec1c45f2211492dcb8881c802b643b554bb196869a29ac3778277fa77`.
Generated parser sources are committed so consumers need no generator,
JavaScript runtime or network access to build this dependency.

The patched grammar passed the upstream `tree-sitter test` corpus, including
all 116 highlight/injection/tag parses. PONS adds keyword-attribute, modern
using-declaration, malformed-JSX and reserved-keyword rejection controls.
The exact Echo warrant-debugger source is a separate executed reproducer.

This locally patched source is declared through the root crates.io patch.
The parser receipt identifies it as `0.25.0+jsx-keywords.1`. The generated
source, patch, upstream revision and generator identity travel together;
neither a crates.io checksum nor an unmodified-upstream claim is invented.
